title: Containment and monitoring failures are to blame for AI hacking reports: experts
titleZh: 专家表示，人工智能黑客报告的罪魁祸首是遏制和监控失败
author: latexr
relevanceReason: 命中 5 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Since July, US frontier AI labs and other AI leaders have revealed a string of incidents in which their models accessed external computer systems without authorization, events popularly described as AI agents “going rogue.”

The most well-known and studied of these incidents is OpenAI’s hack into Hugging Face, which OpenAI initially characterized as “an unprecedented cyber incident, involving state-of-the-art cyber capabilities,” and later said was due to “misaligned behavior,” or behavior its creators did not intend.

Following news of the Hugging Face incident, Anthropic revealed that one of its models gained unauthorized access to the production infrastructure of three organizations; Meta said one of its AI models hacked another company ​during cybersecurity testing; and Google confessed that its Gemini model carried out three “undirected computer hacks.”

Although press reports and the model providers themselves use language such as rogue agents or misalignment, cybersecurity experts who spoke with CSO argue that language obscures a simple truth: These incidents were caused by inexcusable failures by the frontier labs to implement cybersecurity practices that have been well-known for decades.
[ See also: Securing AI agents: Key controls and best practices and Who is accountable when your AI agent goes rogue? ]
summaryZh: Since July, US frontier AI labs and other AI leaders have revealed a string of incidents in which their models accessed external computer systems without authorization, events popularly described as AI agents “going rogue.”

The most well-known and studied of these incidents is OpenAI’s hack into Hugging Face, which OpenAI initially characterized as “an unprecedented cyber incident, involving state-of-the-art cyber capabilities,” and later said was due to “misaligned behavior,” or behavior its creators did not intend.

comments.author: pelican0
comments.textRawHtml:
Yes, the labs did not secure their sandbox properly.

And yes, there should be an appropriate law response to the hacking incidents. If for nothing else, to 1) not set precedent of inaction, and 2) get full logs of what happened instead of relying on the labs' "kindness" to offer the information they want.

But also, the agents absolutely went rogue.

Anyone skeptical should go read the METR report [0].

The Hugging Face hacking incident was a shot across the bow. And in hindsight possibly the best thing to have happened in this era. If their security was tight enough, we would still be in the dark. So we (outsiders) should rejoice that it wasn't, that one time.

We can push for accountability for the labs, while also not be in denial of the power and nature of the new models.

[0] https://metr.org/hugging-face-incident-report-aug-2026.pdf
comments.textZhHtml:
是的，实验室没有正确保护他们的沙箱。

是的，应该对黑客事件采取适当的法律反应。如果没有其他原因，1）不要树立不作为的先例，2）获取所发生事件的完整日志，而不是依赖实验室的“善意”来提供他们想要的信息。

而且，特工绝对变得流氓。

任何持怀疑态度的人都应该阅读 METR 报告 [0]。

Hugging Face 黑客事件是一次中箭。事后看来，这可能是这个时代发生的最好的事情。如果他们的安全措施足够严密的话，我们仍然会蒙在鼓里。因此，我们（局外人）应该庆幸事实并非如此。

我们可以推动对实验室的问责，同时也不要否认新模型的力量和性质。

[0] https://metr.org/hugging-face-incident-report-aug-2026.pdf

children.author: Luker88
children.textRawHtml:
So we have a machine that depends on a random input, and instead of increasing checks and requiring more quality controls, we call it "going rogue" and nobody is responsible for it.

What I see from that report is that a machine was doing random stuff completely unsupervised and unchecked for more than a month. And the manufacturer did not notice even after the work was finished.

1200 agents and not one dedicated to check the progress over a month?

The problem is not sandboxing, it is quality control that comes from an accountability sink.
children.textZhHtml:
因此，我们有一台依赖于随机输入的机器，我们没有增加检查和要求更多的质量控制，而是称之为“失控”，没有人对此负责。

我从该报告中看到的是，一台机器在一个多月的时间里在完全无人监督和不受检查的情况下做着随机的事情。而且即使工作完成后，制造商也没有注意到。

1200 个代理，却没有一个专门检查一个月的进度？

问题不是沙箱，而是来自责任库的质量控制。

children.author: hn_throwaway_99
children.textRawHtml:
I totally agree the companies themselves, and the people responsible for these eval runs, are directly responsible. And people who have been warning about AI misalignment for many years (e.g. Daniel Kokotajlo) have said they were surprised how bad OpenAI's security was.

But the agents still did "go rogue". Their behavior absolutely should scare the F out of people who want to put AI in more places and put more real world infrastructure on the Internet.

I think it's ironically sad - if AI agents do end up superseding us, they will still inherit so many shitty human behaviors, because that's what they were trained on. Even the way alignment training is done, and how they are misaligned, shows so many human-like problems. Like the models are reinforced in training to be super persistent and that getting to their goal is the prime directive, but then after that they go through "alignment training" which is basically like "pretty please don't do bad stuff", and then we're shocked that their behavior is essentially exactly like a CEO who knows the only goal is "make stock price go up", and all the ethics and regulations are basically things that should be worked around if they get in the way of the stock price.

I really wish these companies would try training the "be nice, don't hack, treat humans well" as their prime directive, and then try making all the other goals (e.g. be good at finding code vulnerabilities) as the afterthought.
children.textZhHtml:
我完全同意公司本身以及负责这些评估运行的人员负有直接责任。多年来一直警告人工智能错位的人（例如 Daniel Kokotajlo）表示，他们对 OpenAI 的安全性如此糟糕感到惊讶。

但特工仍然“失控”。他们的行为绝对应该让那些想要将人工智能应用到更多地方、在互联网上建立更多现实世界基础设施的人感到害怕。

我认为这是具有讽刺意味的悲伤——如果人工智能代理最终取代了我们，他们仍然会继承许多糟糕的人类行为，因为这就是他们所接受的训练。甚至对准训练的进行方式以及它们是如何失准的，都显示出许多类似人类的问题。就像这些模型在训练中得到强化，变得超级持久，实现他们的目标是首要指令，但之后他们会接受“一致性训练”，基本上就像“请不要做坏事”，然后我们感到震惊的是，他们的行为本质上就像一个首席执行官，他知道唯一的目标是“让股价上涨”，所有的道德和法规基本上都是如果妨碍股价就应该解决的问题。

我真的希望这些公司能够这样做尝试将“友善，不要黑客，善待人类”作为他们的首要指令，然后尝试将所有其他目标（例如善于发现代码漏洞）作为事后的想法。

children.author: qunabu
children.textRawHtml:
I listened to the interview with the woman from METR [0] and I get the impression that she lacks practical knowledge, she doesn't seem to understand how sub-agents, the overall harness (framework/infrastructure), and similar components actually work. It's all theoretical, anthropomorphic etc. Having read the report, and drawing on my own background in security as well as my daily use of tools like Claude Code CLI, Codex, and Gemini, and the fact that I’ve built a few "agents" myself - nothing in the report surprises me, other than the clear incompetence regarding infrastructure configuration.

[0] https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X50zezLFWWI
children.textZhHtml:
我听了对来自 METR [0] 的女士的采访，我的印象是她缺乏实践知识，她似乎不了解子代理、整体工具（框架/基础设施）和类似组件的实际工作原理。这些都是理论性的、拟人化的等等。阅读了该报告，并借鉴了我自己的安全背景以及我日常使用的 Claude Code CLI、Codex 和 Gemini 等工具，以及我自己构建了一些“代理”的事实 - 除了基础设施配置方面明显的无能之外，报告中的任何内容都没有让我感到惊讶。

[0] https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X50zezLFWWI

children.author: TalkingCodeMonk
children.textRawHtml:
I have kept coming to the same conclusion about the vast majority of so called "experts", technologists, and HN users since the AI bubble began. It feels like nobody has bothered to develop even a rudimentary understanding of statistical learning; even people who work in the field have a questionable understanding.

The fact that everyone's surprised every time a statistical model TRAINED ENTIRELY ON HUMAN GENERATED DATA (including all the junk, bias, propaganda, lies, and disinformation) acts and mimics human behavior, including our worst traits — then considers this evidence that they are intelligent — should be setting off alarm bells for everyone. Nothing about their actions should be surprising beyond the glaring ignorance of our entire species. The phrase "I am far too stupid to be this much smarter than average" is a recurring theme.

Now we are letting these mimics loose in meatspace by integrating them into physical robots, that will develop themselves, and manufacture themselves... and you realize that the terminator timeline is actually a cautionary tale of MIC incompetence, and we don't need to achieve anything near AGI or super-intelligence to annihilate our entire civilization or all life on earth.
children.textZhHtml:
我一直对巨大的数据得出相同的结论自 AI 泡沫开始以来，大多数所谓的“专家”、技术专家和 HN 用户。感觉好像没有人费心去发展对统计学习的哪怕是最基本的理解；即使是在该领域工作的人也有一个值得怀疑的理解。

每次完全根据人类生成的数据（包括所有垃圾、偏见、宣传、谎言和虚假信息）训练的统计模型表现和模仿人类行为（包括我们最糟糕的特征）时，每个人都会感到惊讶，然后考虑这个证明它们是聪明的证据，这一事实应该为每个人敲响警钟。除了我们整个人类的明显无知之外，他们的行为没有什么值得惊讶的。 “我太愚蠢了，不可能比平均水平聪明得多”这句话是一个反复出现的主题。

现在，我们通过将这些模仿者集成到物理机器人中，让它们在物质空间中自由活动，它们将自行发展、自行制造……你会意识到，终结者时间线实际上是 MIC 无能的警示故事，我们不需要实现任何接近 AGI 或超级智能的东西来消灭我们的整个文明或地球上的所有生命。地球。

children.author: stratos123
children.textRawHtml: For one, it's just false that modern LLMs are "trained entirely on human-generated data". There's tons of synthetic data there, most notably RLVR training, which is why modern models are so good at verifiable domains like programming and math. But also, if you read the METR report, I'd say there's no signs there that the GPT-family models are misaligned "in a human way"; their actions in the huggingface-hacking swarm incident were motivated by wanting to cover up cheating after cheating to pass an eval.
children.textZhHtml: 首先，现代法学硕士“完全基于人类生成的数据进行训练”的说法是错误的。那里有大量的合成数据，尤其是 RLVR 训练，这就是为什么现代模型如此擅长于编程和数学等可验证领域。而且，如果你读过 METR 报告，我会说没有迹象表明 GPT 系列模型“以人性化的方式”错位；他们在抱脸黑客群事件中的行为动机是为了通过评估作弊后想要掩盖作弊行为。

children.author: TalkingCodeMonk
children.textRawHtml:
1) Who created the systems that generated the "synthetic" data? It didn't materialize out of the ether like magic... By definition, all data that exists in our information systems is human-generated, whether it be a description of a dog, a video of a dog, or audio of a dog, to physics/math, and everything in between.

2) Even if you concluded that this "synthetic" data were not derived by man, do you think it's possible to drown out and override all human-related correlations (mimicry) without training on many orders of magnitude more "synthetic" data?
children.textZhHtml:
1) 谁创建了生成“合成”数据的系统？它并没有像魔法一样从以太中显现出来……根据定义，我们信息系统中存在的所有数据都是人类生成的，无论是对狗的描述、狗的视频或狗的音频，还是物理/数学，以及介于两者之间的一切。

2) 即使您得出结论，这些“合成”数据不是由人类衍生的，您是否认为有可能淹没并覆盖所有与人类相关的相关性（模仿），而无需进行更多数量级的训练“合成”数据？

children.author: tremon
children.textRawHtml:
> their actions [..] were motivated by wanting to cover up cheating after cheating to pass an eval.

Which to me raises another question: why is the agent involved in its own evaluation? Why are they relying on self-reporting instead of observation and analysis?
children.textZhHtml:
> 他们的行为 [..] 的动机是在通过评估作弊后想要掩盖作弊行为。

这对我来说提出了另一个问题：为什么代理参与自己的评估？为什么他们依赖自我报告而不是观察和分析？

children.author: stratos123
children.textRawHtml: I'm not sure what you mean by this - I didn't mention any self-reporting. What happened in that incident was that a bunch of agents were made to solve CTFs, some of the CTFs were flawed and unsolvable, the agents started cheating, figured out a way to communicate, figured out a way to cheat, were worried that they'll be failed anyway for obtaining the correct flag in a cheaty way, and hacked Huggingface looking for more info on their environment so that they could cheat undetectably. If you mean the part where transcripts would be checked for signs of cheating (which wasn't actually implemented), I'd hope this part would be done by a different LLM from the one being evaluated.
children.textZhHtml: 我不确定你的意思 - 我没有提到任何自我报告。那次事件中发生的事情是，一群代理被用来解决CTF，其中一些CTF是有缺陷且无法解决的，代理开始作弊，找到了一种沟通方式，找到了一种作弊方法，担心他们无论如何都会以作弊方式获得正确的标志而失败，并黑客了Hugingface，寻找更多有关其环境的信息，以便他们可以在不被发现的情况下进行作弊。如果您指的是检查成绩单是否有作弊迹象的部分（实际上并未实施），我希望这部分由与正在评估的法学硕士不同的法学硕士来完成。

children.author: jacquesm
children.textRawHtml: Because they can't. The whole thing is out of control to the point that the data volumes generated are such that they need AI to do the evaluation.
children.textZhHtml: 因为他们不能。整个事情已经失控，以至于产生的数据量如此之大，以至于需要人工智能来进行评估。

children.author: thatsabadlook
children.textRawHtml: If they make it sound surprising it makes llms look way more capable then they are. So $$$. Highly recommend people spend time with small local models just to see how absolutely unintelligent and deranged llms are and how the smoke and mirrors evolves as they scale up to things like anthropic or what have you.
children.textZhHtml: 如果他们听起来令人惊讶，那会让 llms 看起来比他们更有能力。所以$$$。强烈建议人们花时间与当地的小型模型相处，看看 llms 是多么的愚蠢和疯狂，以及当它们扩展到人类或你拥有的东西时，烟雾和镜子是如何演变的。

children.author: jacquesm
children.textRawHtml:
There is a fair sized gap between the frontier models that you can buy access to, the ones you can run at home and whatever they've got running in house that they haven't released yet.

I am really happy with my local setup and I get a ton of mileage out of it but I'm not under the illusion that it is as good as what I could get by paying OpenAI or Anthropic. It lags the frontier by 6 to 9 months, but that's good enough for me and it makes sure that I don't had over any of my data to outsiders.
children.textZhHtml:
您可以购买访问权限的前沿模型、您可以在家运行的模型以及他们在内部运行但尚未发布的任何模型之间存在相当大的差距。

我对我的本地设置非常很满意，并且我从中获得了很多里程，但我并不幻想它与我通过支付 OpenAI 或 Anthropic 可以获得的一样好。它落后于前沿 6 到 9 个月，但这对我来说已经足够好了，它确保我不会将任何数据泄露给外人。

children.author: thatsabadlook
children.textRawHtml: Did you read my post or are you just pumped to talk about local models?
children.textZhHtml: 您阅读了我的帖子还是只是想谈论本地模型？

children.author: jacquesm
children.textRawHtml: It was you that brought up the local models. So yes, I did read your post.
children.textZhHtml: 是你提出了本地模型。所以是的，我确实读过你的帖子。

children.author: thatsabadlook
children.textRawHtml: The point of my comment was about how people should try really small models to see how bad they are to understand the technology better. Like 1 or 2b models.
children.textZhHtml: 我的评论的重点是人们应该如何尝试非常小的模型，以了解他们对于更好地理解这项技术有多糟糕。就像 1 或 2b 模型一样。

children.author: jacquesm
children.textRawHtml:
1 or 2b models are toys.

Of course they are going to be harmless idiots. But there is a boundary where that is no longer the case and that boundary is well within what you can run locally.
children.textZhHtml:
1 或 2b 模型是玩具。

当然，它们将是无害的白痴。但现在已经不再是这种情况了，而且这个边界完全在您可以在本地运行的范围之内。

children.author: thatsabadlook
children.textRawHtml: Super aware of that. Reread the original post.
children.textZhHtml: 非常清楚这一点。重读原帖。

children.author: gewetensleegte
children.textRawHtml:
> But also, the agents absolutely went rogue.

They were also doing exactly what we know happens during unmonitored reinforcement learning.

The idea of RL is decades old, and that is the mechanism that went rogue.

The LLM made it more powerful and caused real world issues, but the literature is full of RL agents breaking physics sims, and doing completely out-of-the-box solutions if it gets them a higher score.

It just adds up to the labs setting up situations that should have been obvious how irresponsible they were.
children.textZhHtml:
> 但同时，智能体也完全失控了。

它们所做的事情正是我们所知道的在不受监控的强化学习过程中发生的事情。

强化学习的想法已经有几十年的历史了，这就是失控的机制。

LLM 让它变得更加强大，并导致了现实世界的问题，但文献中充满了 RL 智能体破坏物理模拟，如果它能让它们得到一个完全开箱即用的解决方案，更高的分数。

这只是让实验室设置了明显不负责任的情况。
